newsitem.title: SURINAM: Suriname slams Dutch for Bouterse arrest request.
newsitem.headline: Suriname slams Dutch for Bouterse arrest request.

text.p: Surinam chastised the Netherlands on Wednesday for seeking to arrest former military leader Desi Bouterse for alleged drug smuggling and said already tense diplomatic relations were wearing thin.

"The Surinamese government expresses its horror with the actions of the Dutch government, which do not befit the usual relations between friendly nations," the Foreign Ministry said in a brief statement.

Dutch Justice Ministry officials said on Wednesday that the Netherlands had asked international police organisation Interpol to arrest Bouterse with an intent to extradite him to face drug trafficking charges.
Bouterse staged military coups in the former Dutch colony in South America in 1980 and 1990.

Officially, he no longer holds public office but his National Democratic Party (NDP) has led a five-party coalition government since elections last September. He was later appointed as an adviser to President Jules Wijdenbosch.
Bouterse has long been distrusted by the Netherlands, where he is held responsible by many for ordering the summary executions in 1982 of 15 opposition leaders.
The decision to arrest him pushed already tense relations between the two nations to the brink and put Wijdenbosch's government in a difficult position, political analysts said.

Surinam, with a population of just over 400,000, depends heavily on development aid from the Dutch government and has close commercial ties with the country. More than 250,000 Surinamese live in the Netherlands.

The Foreign Ministry said the government had still not decided how to respond to the Dutch move against Bouterse. Bouterse's supporters in Surinam said Dutch authorities were using the case to put pressure on Wijdenbosch's government.
"This decision to make Bouterse an internationally wanted criminal has nothing to do with justice and everything to do with politics," NDP Congressman Ronald van Ritter told Reuters.

Allegations of Bouterse's involvement in drug smuggling have surfaced periodically in the Dutch press, but only recently have Dutch authorities confirmed that they were pursuing a criminal investigation of him.
Bouterse, who has previously brushed aside the drug charges as a mild annoyance, made no comments on Wednesday. Calls to his office and home were not returned.
